analysis: The shorter-dilation candidate executed successfully but reduced validation HR@10 from 0.625 to 0.605, a decline of 0.020 (four fewer hits among 200 validation users). Its best checkpoint occurred at epoch 20 of 40. This controlled result does not support replacing the previous dilation schedule with alternating [1, 2]; emphasizing nearby transitions did not improve this run. It does not establish why performance declined. Retain the 0.625 parent as the stronger candidate; no test metrics were used.
code_summary: Schedule-only NextItNet ablation: eight independent residual blocks use dilations [1,2,1,2,1,2,1,2], reducing the theoretical receptive field from 121 to 49 positions. Each block retains two causal kernel-size-3 depthwise convolutions, pointwise mixing, sigmoid value gating, GELU, LayerNorm, dropout, padding masks, and residual addition. The model preserves 64-dimensional item and positional embeddings, MAXLEN=128, dropout=0.2, last-nonpadding candidate scoring, tied item embeddings, and all interfaces. Host training settings remain unchanged.
